In these workshops, we will use the Bioinformatics Core training server. This server provides access to a Linux environment, course data and pre-installed bioinformatics tools. Contact [Shaun Webb](mailto:shaun.webb@ed.ac.uk) for an account.

If you are using the Bioinformatics Core servers, please abide by our user policy and best practices: https://drp-hcb-bioinformatics.github.io/DRP-HCB-Bioinformatics/user_policy.html

If you would like to use your own Linux environment, a list of software versions will be provided at the start of each course. See below for installing software with Conda.

## Terminal applications

To access the server, you will need to use the Terminal application on your local machine. Windows, Mac and Linux computers all have a built in Terminal application. 
There are also many [third party Terminal applications](https://github.com/cdleon/awesome-terminals) if you desire a more stylish or interactive setup.   

## Accessing the server

The `ssh` command is used to connect to a remote server and stands for "secure shell".

`ssh -Y username@bifx-core1.bio.ed.ac.uk`

The `-Y` option allows you to run graphical applications on the server and have them displayed on your local machine. Replace `username` with your university UUN (universal user name).

## Installing software

***Not required if using the Bioinformatics Core servers.***

We recommend [Conda](https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/user-guide/getting-started.html) for installing software on your own Linux environment. Conda is a package manager that allows you to install software and manage dependencies in isolated environments. 

Follow our guide to setting up a Conda environment here:
https://drp-hcb-bioinformatics.github.io/DRP-HCB-Bioinformatics/software.html#managing-your-own-software-tools-and-packages-with-conda

## Project management

It is good practice to keep your work organised in a project folder. This will make it easier to revisit your work in the future. Best practice is to create a new project for each course and keep all of your work in that project folder.

If you are using Conda to install software, it is also good practice to create a new Conda environment for each project. This will help avoid conflicts between software versions and dependencies.
